findings.current: The nightmares began when I started falling asleep the moment I closed my eyes, no matter the time or place.
findings.defect: The draft makes effortless sleep begin alongside the nightmares. The source says he had already been able to fall asleep anywhere, and then began suffering nightmares.
findings.rationale: 잠들었던 describes his prior habit; 시달리기 시작한 것은 is what began a few years ago.
findings.replacement: That was when I, who used to fall asleep as if I’d passed out whenever I closed my eyes, no matter where or when, began having nightmares.
findings.source: 시간과 장소를 불문하고 눈만 감으면 기절하듯 잠들었던 내가 악몽에 시달리기 시작한 것은.

findings.current: A monstrous blaze, born from countless bodies and rivers of blood, completed the hellscape.
findings.defect: “Born from” loses the image of the fire feeding on blood and corpses as fuel.
findings.rationale: 장작 삼아 specifies what fuels the blaze, following the flames’ spread across the pooled blood.
findings.replacement: A monstrous blaze fed on the blood and countless corpses like firewood, completing the hellscape.
findings.source: 무수한 피와 시신을 장작 삼아 일어난 거대한 화마(火魔)가, 이 지옥도를 완성시킨다.

findings.current: The battle in the National Assembly had been a bloody deal: their lives in exchange for tens or hundreds of thousands of others.
findings.defect: The draft leaves the others’ fate unstated, making it sound as though their lives were exchanged for those people rather than for averting their deaths.
findings.rationale: The preceding lines say letting those people live would have caused a larger civil war; their deaths prevented its mass casualties.
findings.replacement: The battle at the National Assembly had been a bloody bargain: their lives to prevent tens, perhaps hundreds, of thousands of others from dying.
findings.source: 그날 국회의사당에서 벌어진 전투는 그들의 목숨과 수만, 수십 만의 희생을 맞바꾼 피의 거래였다.

summary: The draft has a reversed opening timeline and two consequential shifts in the nightmare and its aftermath.
